records.text: The rest of the deeds of Judas, his battles, the brave deeds he performed, and his greatness were not written down, for they were exceedingly many.
The events concerning Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, the purification of the greatest temple and the dedication of the altar,
and also the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and his son Eupator,
and the manifestations from heaven to those who zealously performed brave deeds for Judaism, so that, although few, they plundered the whole land and pursued the barbarian multitudes,
recovered the temple renowned throughout the inhabited world, freed the city, and restored the laws that were about to be abolished, the Lord having become merciful to them with all gentleness—
these things, set forth by Jason of Cyrene in five books, we shall attempt to abridge into one composition.

At that time Alcimus was struck, and his work was obstructed. His mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed, unable to speak another word or give orders concerning his household.

When King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had called against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” Behold, the hand he stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
The altar split, and the fat poured from the altar, according to the portent the man of God had given by the Lord’s word.

King Jeroboam said to the man of God, “Entreat the favor of the Lord your God, and let my hand be restored to me.” The man of God entreated the Lord’s favor, and he restored the king’s hand to him, so it became as it had been before.
All the excess that they did not pay from the revenues as in former years they shall from now on give for the works of the house.

so that they may offer sweet fragrances to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.

Athenobius, the king’s Friend, came to Jerusalem. He saw Simon’s glory, the display of gold and silver vessels, and the large retinue, and was astonished. He reported the king’s words to him.
When the queen of Sheba saw all Solomon’s discernment and the house he had built,
Solomon’s food, the seating of his attendants, the station of his ministers, his clothing, his wine-pourers, and his whole burnt offering which he offered in the Lord’s house, she was beside herself.
She said to King Solomon, “The report I heard in my land about your word and your discernment is true.
I did not believe those speaking to me until I arrived and my eyes saw. Behold, it is not half as they reported to me! You have added good things beyond them, beyond every report I heard in my land.
Blessed are your women! Blessed are these attendants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing all your discernment!

Blessed be the Lord your God, who delighted in you, setting you on Israel’s throne! Because the Lord loves Israel, to establish them for ever, He made you king over them to carry out judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.”

triples.rationale: The first narrator leaves many of Judas's deeds and battles unwritten because of their abundance; the second describes Judas Maccabeus's campaigns as abundant material to be abridged from five books. Both explain selective narration of Judas's history; this does not identify Jason's work as the first narrator's source.

triples.rationale: Alcimus's sanctuary demolition is obstructed when paralysis stops his speech and commands; Jeroboam's hostile gesture against the man speaking at the altar is interrupted by a withered hand. The shared pattern is bodily incapacity limiting hostile authority in a sanctuary setting, with different ailments and outcomes; Jeroboam's hand is restored.

Both provisions assign revenue to Jerusalem's temple work. Demetrius's proposal belongs to the offer explicitly rejected in 1 Maccabees 10:46; the comparison does not establish payment.

triples.rationale: Jonathan's letter says that the Spartan brothers are continually remembered in prayers; Paul's letter likewise speaks of unceasing prayerful remembrance and addresses its recipients as brothers. The correspondence concerns the expressed practice of remembering others in prayer, not the identity or religious standing of the two recipient groups or Paul's adoption of the sacrifices mentioned by Jonathan.

triples.rationale: Jonathan's letter connects sacrifices and prayers with remembrance of the Spartan brothers. Darius's decree supplies offerings so that prayers may be made for the king and his sons. Both link sacrificial worship with intercession for people involved in an external political relationship; a royal directive and Jonathan's statement of practice remain distinct.

triples.relationship: Preservation of official decisions in archives
triples.rationale: Copies of the decision concerning Simon are assigned to the treasury for Simon and his sons. Ezra describes a search in Babylon's treasury libraries and a scroll found in a Median city preserving Cyrus's temple decision. Both connect written decisions concerning temple and priestly affairs with archival preservation, without equating the decrees or their storage locations.

triples.relationship: Foreign visitor's response to a ruler's display
triples.rationale: Athenobius is astonished by Simon's display and large retinue; the queen of Sheba is beside herself on seeing Solomon's household arrangements and attendants. Both narratives describe a foreign visitor's striking response to a ruler's visible establishment. The queen's praise differs from the envoy's hostile mission and subsequent angry report; no identity of vessels or offices is implied.
